value.body: A four-year degree in town and country planning. You study how land, housing, transport, infrastructure and the environment fit together in cities and regions, through planning studios, surveys, GIS and planning law. Graduates work with development authorities, planning and infrastructure consultancies, and research groups, or go on to an M.Plan.

items.label: Course length
items.note: 8 semesters, with studios and site surveys

items.label: Students enrolled

items.label: Professional body
items.note: Membership is asked for in some government planning posts

value.title: How you get in
value.body: JEE Main Paper 2B (B.Planning) for the Schools of Planning and Architecture, NITs and other centrally funded seats through JoSAA. A few institutes and state universities hold their own tests or admit on Class 12 marks. You need Class 12 with Mathematics.

value.title: At a glance
items: Only a small number of colleges offer it, so seats are limited.
Much of the work is with government bodies or consultancies doing government projects.
An M.Plan is common for specialised planning roles.
GIS, surveys and report writing are everyday skills in this field.
